en.question: A Node.js service makes one Claude call per request and blocks the event loop while waiting. Under load, unrelated endpoints become unresponsive. What is the root cause and fix?

options.text: The model is too slow; switching to a smaller model resolves the contention.
options.note: A faster model shortens the block, but the loop is still blocked.

options.text: The context window is exhausted; trimming the prompt frees the event loop.
options.note: Context size affects the API call, not the concurrency model of your process.

options.text: Rate limiting is stalling the calls; adding retries restores responsiveness.
options.note: Retries on a blocking call make the starvation worse.

options.text: Synchronous I/O is starving the loop; use async calls so it stays free to serve.

en.explanation: A single-threaded event loop blocked on network I/O cannot serve anything else. The defect is in how the call is made, not in the model, the prompt, or the limits.
